description: Renovate is the ONLY dependency bot on this repository.

WHY ONE BOT: this repo previously ran Renovate and Dependabot side by side, with .github/dependabot.yml reduced to `open-pull-requests-limit: 0` purely so the two would not fight over the same lockfile. Two bots that must be configured not to collide is a maintenance tax with no upside, and on a public repo it doubles the visible PR noise. Dependabot's config was deleted and Renovate kept, because Renovate is the one carrying real intent here: an opt-in allowlist, grouping, a schedule, and per-rule reasoning. It also natively understands SHA-pinned GitHub Actions, which is now load-bearing (see the github-actions rule below).

WHAT REPLACED DEPENDABOT: the `vulnerabilityAlerts` block below. Renovate reads GitHub's own advisory data, so security fixes still arrive automatically — they just arrive from one bot instead of two. Repository setting to match: Settings ▸ Code security ▸ leave Dependabot ALERTS on (they cost nothing and feed Renovate), and turn Dependabot SECURITY UPDATES off so it stops opening a competing PR for the same advisory.

CLOSED TO CONTRIBUTION: this project is source-available and does not accept outside pull requests. Renovate's PRs are not an exception to that — they are automated maintenance opened by a bot against the maintainer's own repo, which is why every one of them is labelled `automated` (excluded from the generated release notes in .github/release.yml) and carries an explicit header saying so.

WHAT ACTUALLY GATES THE AGENT-CLI PR: `pnpm check:runtime-pins` (preflight, on both ubuntu and macOS). An earlier version of this file claimed the gate was `pnpm test:git + pnpm models:verify --strict`; that was FALSE for the only direction Renovate moves. models:verify's CLI check fires only when the bundled CLI is OLDER than a curated model needs, so a forward bump satisfies it trivially — and test:adapters replays committed fixtures through unchanged translator source, so its output is bump-invariant. check:runtime-pins closes that hole by resolving the Claude platform binary and executing its own `--version`, which is why a renamed or dropped platform package now fails on the PR rather than post-merge in release-alpha. check:codex-pin remains the Codex protocol-triple gate. Staleness itself is reported weekly by the runtime-drift job in scheduled.yml.
prHeader: Automated maintenance opened by Renovate. This repository is source-available and closed to outside contribution; bot upgrade PRs are the only non-maintainer PRs that are ever merged here.

packageRules.description: Opt-in per package: this repo only automates the bundled agent-CLI pins for now. Disable everything else so Renovate doesn't flood the repo. Broaden later by removing this rule (or scoping it).

Bundled agent runtimes — shipped executables, not ordinary libraries. A bump to @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk swaps the actual claude-code binary the app stages (its claudeCodeVersion); @openai/codex swaps the Codex binary and desyncs the protocol triple; @cursor/sdk IS the entire Cursor backend (the sole and only Cursor runtime — there is no CLI/ACP fallback, see src/engine/agents/adapters/cursor-sdk/index.ts). All three are pinned EXACTLY, not by range: a range lets a lockfile refresh swap a shipped binary with no reviewed diff. Grouped into one weekly PR, labeled, and NOT auto-merged — a new SDK can carry protocol/API changes the adapters must adapt to, so a human reviews the green PR. SCHEDULE IS A WHOLE DAY, NOT A MORNING: `* * * * 1` = any time Monday (cron, in the `timezone` above), widened from `before 6am on monday` on 2026-08-04. A schedule is not a promise that Renovate RUNS then — it only permits a run that happens to land inside it. The hosted app was observed running this repo at 00:26:26 UTC, and 6am Asia/Kolkata is 00:30 UTC: a 3m34s margin. Any drift in when Mend schedules the run silently costs a full week, and the miss is invisible — the dashboard just keeps saying 'awaiting schedule'. A whole-day window trades a tighter delivery time (which nothing here needs) for a 24-hour target the run cannot realistically miss.

GitHub Actions are pinned to full commit SHAs (with the version in a trailing comment) so a compromised upstream can't repoint a tag into a job that holds the Developer ID cert and the R2 write keys. A SHA pin only stays safe if something bumps it, and that something is this rule — without it the pins silently rot into permanently-outdated code. Grouped into one monthly PR so the pin refresh is a single reviewable diff rather than a trickle, and never auto-merged: the whole point of a SHA pin is that a human looks at what the new SHA is. SCHEDULE IS A WHOLE DAY, NOT A MORNING: `* * 1 * *` = any time on the 1st (cron, in the `timezone` above), widened from `before 6am on the first day of the month` on 2026-08-04 for the reason spelled out in the agent-CLI rule above — a 3m34s margin against the observed run time, where a miss costs a MONTH rather than a week. Whole-day windows are the shape Renovate's own presets use for day-granular schedules (`schedule:quarterly` is `* * 1 */3 *`), so this is the documented idiom, not a workaround. A missed window here is the worst kind: this rule is the only thing that stops the SHA pins rotting, so silently skipping a month directly weakens the supply-chain posture the pins exist to provide.

Runtime versions that happen to live inside workflow files are parity pins, not action pins, so they are carved back out of the rule above. `node-version: 22` must match the runtime the code actually ships on — backend/Dockerfile deploys the control plane on node:22-alpine, and the desktop app's Electron bundles its own Node — and the preflight `postgres:16` service must match the Railway Postgres major the migrations actually run against (backend/README.md documents 16 as the tested target). Letting the monthly actions group bump these makes CI validate a runtime nothing ships on: tests passing on Node 24 / PG 18 prove nothing about Node 22 / PG 16 in production. Bump them by hand, in the same PR that moves the real runtime (Dockerfile, engines, @types/node, or the Railway database).

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes bypass the opt-in allowlist above. `enabled: true` here overrides the `matchPackageNames: [*] / enabled: false` rule for advisory-driven updates only, so a vulnerable transitive dependency still gets a PR even though routine version bumps for that package are muted. This is the capability that made Dependabot worth keeping before it was removed; unscheduled on purpose, because an advisory should not wait for Monday.
